spec_match.rationale: The page claims to show 'every corner-shape value' but lists an invented 'straight' keyword (CSS.supports false even on Chromium 141, which ships corner-shape) while omitting the spec's real 'square' keyword and the superellipse() function that squircle/bevel etc. are defined in terms of.

interactive.rationale: The radius slider live-updates all six swatches via border-radius plus per-swatch corner-shape, and the readout narrates the radius-zero collapse case.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises 'every corner-shape value on the same box', which the value-set defect makes untrue; the bevel/scoop/notch/squircle comparison it promises does render correctly here.

edge_cases.rationale: Radius zero, per-value support badges, and the no-corner-shape-at-all fallback narration are all present and correct.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite proves the shorthand contracts well, but nothing in it pins the corner-shape keyword vocabulary, which is exactly where this page drifted from the spec.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: banner reports '5 of 6 shapes are supported here'; slider driven to 0 ('every shape is a square corner' narration) and to 60px; swatch states read supported×5 + 'not supported here' for straight; console clean, no exceptions, screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Renders log and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert('gallery-rendered', …) with radius and supported counts.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, unsupported swatches recolour box and state text together, slider has a 44px hit target, no static-card pattern.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled slider with visible value, per-swatch support state as text, aria-live readout; swatches are non-interactive display elements.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; the auto-fit gallery wraps to narrow columns with legible captions in the mobile screenshot.

openQuestions.title: Fix the value set: 'straight' is not a corner-shape value, 'square' and superellipse() are
openQuestions.detail: CSS Borders 4 defines <corner-shape-value> as round | scoop | bevel | notch | square | squircle | superellipse(). Verified on Chromium 141: CSS.supports('corner-shape','square')===true and 'superellipse(2)'===true while 'straight'===false — so the gallery permanently shows a red 'not supported here' badge for a keyword that does not exist in any engine, which is a false statement about the browser, and the description given for 'straight' ('no shaping at all') is actually what 'square' does. Replace the straight swatch with square, and add a superellipse(k) swatch (a small k slider would show the round↔squircle↔square continuum, the most instructive part of the spec). The same wrong list is in ../corner-builder/.

summary: Mechanically the gallery is sound — verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/css-corner-shorthand-properties/shape-gallery/, where corner-shape itself is supported and five swatches genuinely render distinct silhouettes with the radius-zero collapse working, clean console and no overflow on either class. But the page's core claim ('every corner-shape value') is wrong: it ships an invented 'straight' keyword whose permanent not-supported badge misreports every browser, and it omits the real 'square' keyword and superellipse(). Feature /conformance/ route ran 1 pass / 7 fail — those failures are honest pre-155 shorthand gaps, unrelated to the vocabulary defect.
